ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, all quadrilaterals in the figure are squares, and the triangle is a right-angled triangle. The areas of the two smaller squares are respectively 1 and 2. What is the area of the largest square?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Since the areas of the two small squares are respectively 1 and 2,\\
it follows that they are the squares of the two legs of a right triangle,\\
thus, according to the Pythagorean theorem, we have: $S_{\text{large square}}=S_{\text{area of the small square is 1}}+S_{\text{area of the small square is 2}}=\boxed{3}$
